+    @staticmethod
+    def _is_call_with_generator_or_list_comprehension(call, func_name):
+        """Return True if the Call node is a call to *func_name* with a
+        single generator expression or list comprehension argument, e.g.
+        ``all(x for x in y)`` or ``all([x for x in y])``."""
+        return (
+            isinstance(call.func, ast.Name)
+            and call.func.id == func_name
+            and len(call.args) == 1
+            and not call.keywords
+            and isinstance(call.args[0], (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp))
+        )
+
     def visit_Call_35(self, call):
         """
         visit `ast.Call` nodes on Python3.5 and after
         """
+        if self._is_call_with_generator_or_list_comprehension(call, "all"):
+            return self._visit_all(call)
         new_func, func_expl = self.visit(call.func)
         arg_expls = []
         new_args = []
@@ -991,6 +1006,33 @@ warn_explicit(

+    def _visit_all(self, call):
+        """Special rewrite for the builtin all() function, see #5062.
+
+        Rewrites a call to ``all()`` whose only argument is a generator
+        expression or a list comprehension into a ``for`` loop with a
+        plain ``assert`` for each item, so that when the assertion fails
+        the offending item and its explanation are shown, instead of just
+        ``False``.
+        """
+        gen_exp = call.args[0]
+        assertion_module = ast.Module(
+            body=[ast.Assert(test=gen_exp.elt, msg=None, lineno=1, col_offset=1)]
+        )
+        AssertionRewriter(module_path=None, config=None).run(assertion_module)
+        for_loop = ast.For(
+            iter=gen_exp.generators[0].iter,
+            target=gen_exp.generators[0].target,
+            body=assertion_module.body,
+            orelse=[],
+        )
+        set_location(for_loop, call.lineno, call.col_offset)
+        self.statements.append(for_loop)
+        # Return True: if we got here it means every item in the iterable
+        # satisfied the assertion (otherwise the loop above would already
+        # have raised an AssertionError with a meaningful explanation).
+        return _NameConstant(True), ""
+
     def visit_Starred(self, starred):
